text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc was still in negotiations with six leading lenders on Tuesday, after a mandate for two court-appointed mediators expired on midnight Monday.

"The negotiations are continuing," a Eurotunnel spokeswoman told Reuters. "It's very, very hard and every millimetre counts. It's rather like 'Mission: Impossible'" she said, referring to the cult action film and TV series.
French co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle carried on the talks with the lenders through Monday night and was set to continue on Tuesday. There was no indication when the shares would requote.

The mediation role of Robert Badinter and Lord Wakeham ran out on Monday and was not extended by the president of the Paris commercial court, Jean-Pierre Mattei, who appointed them in February to help negotiate a refinancing of Eurotunnel's debt.
The spokeswoman confirmed that the positions of the banks and Eurotunnel were getting closer but no agreement had been reached.
"It's true the positions are getting closer. There are the beginnings of the two sides coming together," she said.
But as the positions came closer, the room for manoeuvre grew much smaller. "The talks are very intense and difficult," she said.
Eurotunnel did not plan to make a statement on when its shares would requote until the situation was clarified, the spokeswoman said.
The shares were suspended in London, Paris and Brussels on Monday to avoid speculation and the creation of a "false market" in the stock while the talks were going on.

The court president has the discretion to allow the negotiations to continue if it appeared there were hopes of an agreement. "He could allow a period of a few hours or a few days," the spokeswoman said.
